Building a Design System — Figma → Claude

384 component families spread across 41 Figma pages, readable only by the person who drew them. The work was turning that into one published system engineers, PMs and marketing can build from without opening a design file.

Tools

Figma, Claude

My role

Design system owner

Deliverable

Published component library

Credit

GyanDhan

Context

Components existed. A system didn't. GyanDhan's Figma file held 384 component families across 41 pages, sitting alongside 85 Rails ViewComponents already in the codebase and 212 un-componentised partials still hand-built per page. Most of the 384 were the same component re-drawn for a new screen: eleven separate card families, four duplicate icon sets, a dozen numbered Frame 12726… fragments with no name a search would ever find. Every new page started by re-drawing what already existed, because nothing lived anywhere a second designer could discover it.

Approach

Count what exists before you draw anything new. Three sources went into one audit (the Figma kit, the live website, and both the merged and unmerged branches of the Rails components), so every family got a decision: consolidate, build, or skip with a reason.

Inventory
384 Figma families, 85 built components, and 50+ live website pages audited side by side, with real instance counts.
3 sources
Consolidate
Eleven card families became one MasterCard family of eight presets.
11 → 1
Skip, with reasons
Raw shapes, bitmaps, and device shells logged as intentional skips, not oversights.
logged
Fill the gaps
Charts, Pagination, and Modal added against Blade, Carbon, and Material 3 — components the Figma file never had.
new

New in Claude

131 components, well past what the Figma file shipped. Charts, overlays, and a full feedback set didn't exist in the kit at all; they're built here against real precedent, on the same tokens as everything migrated over.

Charts

DonutChart, TrendChart, GaugeChart: no chart family existed in the kit.

Overlays

Modal, Popup, AuthModal, FilterPanel: unspecced in Figma, built and documented here.

Feedback

Toast, Skeleton, EmptyState, AlertBar: filled from the shared-partials backlog.

Try the prototype

Rendered from the Claude-built library, not a screenshot. Switch between input states, MasterCard presets, and the chart family below. Drag the sliders and trigger the overlays to see the components respond live.

My role vs. the tool

Figma stayed the space for auditing and comparing what existed. Claude became the space for testing a component against real screens faster than I could hand-build each variant, so I could spend my time on judgment calls (which eleven cards actually collapse into one, what a chart family needs to cover, where a skip is the right call) instead of redrawing components.

Outcome

One published library instead of a file only its author could read. Engineers, PMs, and marketing can now pull a component without opening Figma or asking the designer what a frame was for.
